channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: High-level aviation safety conference held in Moscow
item.description: A high-level conference on flight safety was held in Moscow on November 26, 2026, initiated by the Interstate Aviation Committee (IAC). The event marked the 35th anniversary of the Agreement on Civil Aviation and Airspace Use and the establishment of the IAC. Representatives from aviation authorities, airlines, and airports from Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan participated.

item.title: Medication and doctor fees continue to rise in Kazakhstan
item.description: In October 2026, healthcare inflation in Kazakhstan rose by 14.7% compared to the same month in 2025. Specialist doctor services increased by 16%, outpatient services by 12.8%, and various medical procedures also saw price hikes. Pharmaceutical products prices grew by 19.4% year-on-year, with common medications like Aspirin and No-Shpa becoming significantly more expensive.

item.title: Forensic experts trained in documenting torture and violence in Bishkek
item.description: Twenty-six forensic medical experts in Bishkek underwent training on documenting violence, torture, and ill-treatment. The course, held from November 23-24, focused on practical skills for describing injuries, photography, evaluating examination results, and preparing expert reports. Participants had previously received theoretical knowledge online. The training was supported by the British Embassy and UNFPA.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Link Jet Fuel Prices to Global Rates, Offer New Airline Incentives
item.description: Starting in 2027, Uzbekistan will set jet fuel prices based on global averages, exempting them from excise tax and applying a zero VAT rate. Airlines will also benefit from extended customs duty exemptions on spare parts until 2040 and zero VAT on aircraft leases. These measures aim to expand the national fleet to 250 aircraft by 2030.

item.title: Tashkent Suburban Bus Routes to Transition to New System
item.description: Bus routes connecting Tashkent with its agglomeration, up to 20 kilometers long, will adopt a gross contract system. New financing mechanisms will be developed to boost bus transport from remote regions. Companies operating at least 100 buses will receive tax deductions. The Tashkent metro plans to import 28 new five-car trains by 2028.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Creates Equal Conditions for Local and Foreign Businesses
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established equal conditions and support measures for both domestic and foreign businesses, according to Artem Novikov, Chairman of the Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund. Speaking at an investment forum, Novikov noted a significant increase in investment activity and joint projects. The fund offers preferential financing and investment agreements for projects exceeding $10 million.

item.title: Kazakh Banks to Fund Over $1 Billion Acquisition of Altynalmas by Businessman Mutalip
item.description: Several Kazakh banks, led by Halyk Bank, will provide over $1 billion to businessman Shakhmurat Mutalip for his acquisition of the gold mining company Altynalmas, valued at approximately $3 billion. Regulatory changes now permit larger loans to mining firms. Mutalip may also acquire Kazzinc Ltd. from Glencore for around $5 billion.

item.title: Suspect in 10-year-old Astana robbery extradited from Spain to Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, with Interpol's assistance and support from the Kazakh embassy in Spain, extradited a foreign national wanted for a 2014 Astana robbery. The suspect, who allegedly prepared masks and gloves with accomplices, entered the victim's home through a window, used force, and stole money and valuables. One accomplice was previously sentenced to 11 years.

item.title: Kazakhstan to open 10,338 polling stations for maslikhat elections on November 29
item.description: Kazakhstan will open 10,338 polling stations for the upcoming maslikhat elections scheduled for November 29. Voters will cast their ballots at these designated locations across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan opens new center for road construction technology implementation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited a new scientific-practical center in Tashkent focused on implementing modern road construction technologies and training specialists. The center includes a training ground, digital systems for road monitoring, and laboratories for material testing.

item.title: Trump asked Putin to stop military aggression in Europe, met in China
item.description: US President Trump stated he asked Russian leader Putin to halt military aggression across Europe during a meeting in China last week. Trump expressed hope this would pave the way for a quicker resolution to the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $5 Billion Aerocity Project Near New Tashkent Airport
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement a $5 billion Aerocity project adjacent to the new Tashkent International Airport. The project, covering 1300 hectares, will be developed under a public-private partnership. It aims to create an integrated ecosystem with logistics centers, hotels, and residential areas.

item.title: Free Public Transport Offered in Several Kazakh Cities for Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Several cities in Kazakhstan will offer free public transport on November 29 to facilitate citizen access to polling stations for the extraordinary maslikhat elections. This initiative aims to encourage voter turnout.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to host the Futsal Asia Cup in 2028
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has been selected to host the Futsal Asia Cup in 2028. The decision was made at a meeting of the Asian Football Confederation's Futsal Committee in Phuket, Thailand. The continental tournament is scheduled to take place from January 24 to February 6, 2028. This will be Kyrgyzstan's first experience hosting the final stage of the Futsal Asia Cup.

item.title: Over 10,000 polling stations to operate for Kazakhstan's local council elections
item.description: More than 10,000 polling stations will be open for the elections of deputies to local councils in Kazakhstan. Voting begins at 6:00 AM in 101 stations and at 7:00 AM in all others. The Central Election Commission stated that the electoral campaign is proceeding according to plan, with over 12.6 million voters registered.

item.title: Uzbek President Stresses Quality and Modern Technology in Road Construction
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need for prioritizing quality and modern technologies in road construction. He stated that Uzbekistan needs durable roads built with proper techniques, rather than cheap ones requiring frequent repairs. Starting next March, the Fergana refinery will produce polymer bitumen, a material that extends road lifespan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Imports from China 22 Times Higher Than Exports
item.description: In January-September 2026, China remained Kyrgyzstan's largest supplier, while Switzerland became the main export market. Kyrgyzstan imported $4.19 billion from China, exporting only $195.3 million, a 22-fold difference. Trade with Russia also showed a significant imbalance, with imports exceeding exports. Imports from Uzbekistan also increased substantially.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Key Changes for Citizens Starting December 1, 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan will see changes in loan restructuring rules, increased mobile and delivery service prices, and digital marking for clothing and jewelry starting December 1, 2026. The National Bank will announce its final base rate decision for the year. Some workers will receive salary increases, and additional trains and international flights will be launched.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mountains Equipped with New Camera Traps for Wildlife Monitoring
item.description: NABU Kyrgyzstan, in collaboration with state ecological organizations, continues to deploy camera traps in Kyrgyzstan's mountains. Recent installations in the Karakol State Nature Park aim to monitor wildlife and study their habitats. Training sessions on using the equipment were also provided.

item.title: Almaty Surgeons Successfully Operate on Infant with Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia
item.description: Surgeons in Almaty have successfully performed a minimally invasive surgery on a three-month-old infant suffering from a severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The condition caused internal organs to compress the baby's underdeveloped lung. The procedure restored proper organ placement and allowed the lung to expand.

item.title: Chechen activist in Kazakhstan fears torture if extradited, reportedly damages cell
item.description: Chechen activist Mansur Movlayev, detained in Almaty, has appealed to the public, fearing torture and death if extradited to Russia. Reports suggest he damaged a surveillance camera in his detention cell. His lawyers believe this may be an attempt to remain in Kazakhstan by facing charges for property damage.

item.title: Uzbek President Visits Road Committee's Scientific Center
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the scientific and practical center of the Automobile Roads Committee. He emphasized the importance of effectively utilizing the center's capabilities to train qualified engineers and specialists for the road sector. Mirziyoyev also highlighted the need for modern technologies to improve road construction quality and operational efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan Minority Shareholders Propose State Asset Reform
item.description: Amidst recent arrests of executives, the Association of Minority Shareholders (QAMS) proposed reforms for state asset management in Kazakhstan. QAMS suggests selling 10% of Samruk-Kazyna, reducing state stakes in national companies to 51%, and limiting government officials' roles on boards. The association argues the current system fosters corruption and weakens minority shareholder influence.

item.title: Trump Urges Putin to Halt Military Aggression in Europe for Peace Deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump has called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to cease all military offensive actions in Europe. Trump stated this request was made during recent talks in China, aiming to pave the way for a peace agreement and end the Ukraine war. He described the conflict as bloody, causing thousands of deaths monthly. Washington has postponed decisions on reviewing its military presence in Europe.

item.title: CEC Members Educate Students on Election Procedures in Manas and Batken
item.description: Members of Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission (CEC) met with university students in Manas, Sülüktü, and Batken cities to inform them about their electoral rights and voting procedures. Discussions covered participation in elections, the role of young voters, and the application of election laws in daily life. Students asked questions and received information on the capabilities of modern election systems. The CEC's outreach campaign continues until December 11.

item.title: Long Wait Times for Children at Almaty Infectious Diseases Hospital Explained
item.description: Almaty's Children's Clinical Infectious Diseases Hospital attributes long wait times to a high volume of non-hospitalization cases and the need for additional examinations. Many parents bring children directly to emergency rooms, bypassing clinics, especially at night. Factors contributing to delays include multiple children per family, diagnostic tests, waiting for results, and patients from nearby rural areas seeking specialized care.

item.title: UN Agency Warns Restrictions on Female Aid Workers Endanger Afghan Women and Girls
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) states that restrictions on Afghan female aid workers increase the risk of women and girls being deprived of life-saving assistance, vital information, and safety. OCHA urges that female aid workers be allowed access to those in need, emphasizing that no woman or girl should be denied aid.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Achieves Over 10% Annual GDP Growth Following Six Years of Reforms
item.description: Since 2020, Kyrgyzstan has transformed its political, economic, and social development, moving from a budget deficit to achieving over 10% annual GDP growth. The country is now a global leader in stable economic growth, attracting increased foreign and domestic investment in infrastructure and industry. These accelerated reforms have modernized the political system and strengthened governance.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Doubling State-Funded Lawyer Fees
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a proposal to double the fees for lawyers providing state-guaranteed legal aid. The initiative, aimed at improving access to legal services, seeks to increase lawyer participation, especially in remote areas. The proposed changes would affect criminal, civil, and administrative cases, requiring an additional 161.1 million soms from the state budget.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Allowing SMS Notifications for Employee Dismissals
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering amendments to its Labor Code that would allow employers to notify employees of termination via SMS, email, or messengers. This change aims to simplify the dismissal process, particularly when employees are absent or refuse to receive a dismissal order. The notification must state the date and grounds for termination.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China Discuss Energy Grid Integration and Cross-Border Power Line by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and China have discussed integrating their energy systems and building a cross-border power line for electricity imports from China. The new infrastructure is proposed for commissioning in December 2027. This was reported by the Ministry of Energy of Kyrgyzstan following a meeting in Qingdao.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Introducing Investment Prosecutor to Protect Investor Rights
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is planning to pilot an investment prosecutor system to safeguard investor rights. This initiative was announced by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers following a meeting with entrepreneurs. The goal is to ensure a unified approach and prompt resolution of issues for investors.

item.title: Baiterek Holding plans to direct 8 trillion tenge to the economy by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Baiterek National Investment Holding plans to allocate 8 trillion tenge to the economy by 2027. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed the holding to increase work efficiency and avoid formal approaches. The plan includes investments in manufacturing, infrastructure, and agriculture, as well as the commissioning of approximately 2.7 million square meters of housing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's business sector unprepared for increased waste recycling fees
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Environment has proposed revising waste recycling norms, which directly impact the extended producer responsibility (EPR) fees. The proposal suggests maintaining 2026 levels for 2027 and postponing the 80% target achievement from 2030 to 2032, citing business concerns. Specific recycling rates for different product groups are outlined for the coming years.

item.title: Tajikistan and Poland Companies Discuss Cooperation at Dushanbe Business Forum
item.description: A business forum between Tajikistan and Poland was held in Dushanbe on November 26, 2026, attended by over 60 Tajik and 15 Polish companies. The event aimed to expand trade and economic cooperation, strengthen business ties, and establish mutually beneficial partnerships across various sectors including construction, manufacturing, and agriculture.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allow Private Companies Access to 'Silent' Pensioner Funds
item.description: Private management companies in Kazakhstan will gain access to pension assets of 'silent' contributors who have not chosen a manager. This expansion of opportunities will allow either individual transfers by contributors or a mandate-based approach from the National Bank. The changes are expected to significantly stimulate the development of Kazakhstan's stock market.

item.title: Kazakhstan Warns of Flamingo Disappearance Risk Due to Drone Flights
item.description: Kazakh authorities are urging bloggers to refrain from using drones near large gatherings of pink flamingos. The Committee of Forestry and Wildlife warned that regular disturbance could cause birds to abandon their habitats. Drone noise and proximity cause stress, hindering feeding and rest. Drone flights are prohibited within one kilometer of flocking bird habitats.

item.title: Tashkent plans $5 billion Aerocity complex near new international airport
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to build a $5 billion multifunctional Aerocity complex on 800 hectares near the future Tashkent International Airport. The complex will include logistics centers, hotels, and retail spaces. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the project during a meeting with investors. The airport itself will occupy 1,300 hectares, with international companies involved in its development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan state bodies urge citizens to support presidential candidates via "Tunduk"
item.description: Several Kyrgyz ministries and state institutions are encouraging citizens to support presidential candidates through the "Tunduk" app. The head of state's affairs manager also called for active participation in signature collection. Officials emphasize "Tunduk" as a secure platform, preventing political manipulation and ensuring privacy of supporters. Candidates need 30,000 signatures by December 8.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Digital Technology to Prevent Falsification of Medical Records
item.description: Kazakhstan is increasing the use of digital technologies to prevent the falsification of patient medical records. Over 160 million medical visits have been confirmed via Face ID and the 'Digital Documents' service in eGov Mobile, accounting for 72.2% of registered visits. This system verifies patient identity and presence, preventing the entry of unreceived services. The project began in Astana in 2024 and is expanding nationwide.
